question: The selling price of 50 books is equal to the cost price of 39 books. Find the loss or gain percentage.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given that the Selling Price (SP) of 50 books is equal to the Cost Price (CP) of 39 books.

Convert this into a ratio: SP / CP = 39 / 50.

Assuming CP is 50 units and SP is 39 units, there is a loss since CP > SP.

Loss = 50 − 39 = 11 units.

Loss % = (11 ÷ 50) × 100 = 22%.

**∴ The correct answer is 22% loss.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

SP of 50 books = CP of 39 books

**Formula Used:**

Loss = CP − SP

Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100

 
 Cost Price (CP) = 50 units

 
 Selling Price = 39 units

 
 Loss = 11

 
• 
 
• 
 
• 

 Loss % = (11 ÷ 50) × 100 = 22%

**Calculations:**

⇒ 50 × SP = 39 × CP

⇒ SP / CP = 39 / 50

⇒ Let CP = 50 units and SP = 39 units.

⇒ Loss = 50 − 39 = 11 units.

⇒ Loss % = (11 ÷ 50) × 100

⇒ Loss % = 11 × 2 = 22%

**∴ The correct answer is 22% loss.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Basics

Profit = SP − CP and Loss = CP − SP. Both percentages are always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless specifically stated otherwise.

Dishonest Dealer

If a dealer claims to sell goods at CP but uses false weight, Gain % = [Error ÷ (True Weight − Error)] × 100.

Successive Discount

If two successive discounts of a% and b% are given on an article, the equivalent single discount is given by the formula (a + b − ab ÷ 100)%.
